at ramme.explanation: "At ramme" means "to hit". To say you hit what you aimed at, say: "Jeg ramte bolden" (I hit the ball). To say something hurts people, it also means "to affect": "Krisen ramte mange" (The crisis hit many people).

sentence.da: Kan du **ramme** målet med bolden?
sentence.en: Can you hit the target with the ball?

at ramme plet.explanation: "At ramme plet" means "to hit the mark". Literally, it is "to hit spot", since "en plet" means "a spot". To say a description was exactly right, say: "Din beskrivelse ramte plet" (Your description hit the mark).

sentence.da: Hun vil **ramme plet** med sit gæt.
sentence.en: She will hit the mark with her guess.

at rapportere.explanation: "At rapportere" means "to report". It comes from "en rapport" (a report). To say what a newspaper tells, add "om" (about): "Avisen rapporterer om ulykken" (The paper reports on the accident). To say you told someone about a mistake, say: "Jeg rapporterede fejlen" (I reported the error).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **rapportere** til min leder hver mandag.
sentence.en: I have to report to my manager every Monday.

at rasle.explanation: "At rasle" means "to rattle". To say keys make a noise in your pocket, say: "Nøglerne rasler i lommen" (The keys rattle in the pocket). To say dry leaves make a sound, it means "to rustle": "Tørre blade rasler i vinden" (Dry leaves rustle in the wind).

sentence.da: Mønterne kan **rasle** i dåsen, når jeg ryster den.
sentence.en: The coins can rattle in the tin when I shake it.

at rationalisere.explanation: "At rationalisere" means "to rationalize". To say an organization makes its work faster and cheaper, say: "Kommunen har rationaliseret administrationen" (The municipality has streamlined the administration). To say someone invents reasons for what they did, say: "Han rationaliserer sit valg" (He rationalizes his choice).

sentence.da: Firmaet vil **rationalisere** produktionen for at spare penge.
sentence.en: The company wants to rationalize production in order to save money.

at reagere.explanation: "At reagere" means "to react". To say someone reacted fast, say: "Hun reagerede hurtigt" (She reacted quickly). To name what you react to, add "på" (to): "Han reagerer på kritik" (He reacts to criticism).

sentence.da: Jeg ved ikke, hvordan jeg skal **reagere**.
sentence.en: I do not know how I should react.

at realisere.explanation: "At realisere" means "to realize", as in making a plan come true. To say a project was carried out, say: "Vi har realiseret projektet" (We have carried out the project). To become aware of something, use "at indse" instead: "Jeg indser, at jeg tog fejl" (I realize that I was wrong).

sentence.da: Hun vil **realisere** sin drøm om at åbne en café.
sentence.en: She wants to realize her dream of opening a cafe.

at redde.explanation: "At redde" means "to save or rescue". To say someone was saved from danger, add "fra" (from): "De reddede ham fra at drukne" (They saved him from drowning). To save money, use "at spare" instead: "Jeg sparer penge" (I save money).

sentence.da: Brandmanden kan **redde** hunden fra branden.
sentence.en: The firefighter can save the dog from the fire.

at rede håret.explanation: "At rede håret" means "to comb one's hair". To say you make the bed, the same verb "rede" is used: "at rede sengen" (to make the bed).

sentence.da: Hun vil **rede håret** med en kam.
sentence.en: She wants to comb her hair with a comb.

at rede seng.explanation: "At rede seng" means "to make the bed". To say you do it every morning, use "sengen" (the bed): "Jeg reder sengen hver morgen" (I make the bed every morning).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **rede seng**, når jeg står op.
sentence.en: I want to make the bed when I get up.

at redegøre for.explanation: "At redegøre for" means "to account for". The small word "for" must always follow it. To say you explain in order what happened, say: "Han redegjorde for ulykken" (He gave an account of the accident).

sentence.da: Du skal **redegøre for** pengene, og chefen vil se kvitteringerne.
sentence.en: You must account for the money, and the boss wants to see the receipts.

at redigere.explanation: "At redigere" means "to edit". It is the verb for "en redaktør" (an editor). To say you change a text, say: "Hun redigerer artiklen" (She is editing the article).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **redigere** videoen, før jeg lægger den på nettet.
sentence.en: I have to edit the video before I put it online.

at reducere.explanation: "At reducere" means "to reduce". To say a shop has lowered the price, use "reduceret pris" (reduced price): "Alle jakker er til reduceret pris" (All jackets are at a reduced price).

sentence.da: Man kan **reducere** sit strømforbrug ved at slukke lyset.
sentence.en: You can reduce your electricity use by turning off the light.

at referere.explanation: "At referere" means "to refer or report". To point back to something already said, add "til" (to): "Jeg refererer til din mail" (I am referring to your email). To retell in short what someone said or wrote, use it with no "til": "Han refererede artiklen for os" (He told us what the article said).

sentence.da: Hun skal **referere** mødet for dem, der ikke var der.
sentence.en: She has to report on the meeting for those who were not there.

at reflektere.explanation: "At reflektere" means "to reflect". To say you think deeply about something, add "over" (on): "Jeg reflekterer over mit valg" (I am reflecting on my choice). To say a surface sends light back, add no small word: "Sneen reflekterer lyset" (The snow reflects the light).

sentence.da: Du bør **reflektere** over, hvad du har lært i dag.
sentence.en: You should reflect on what you have learned today.

at regere.explanation: "At regere" means "to govern or rule". To say someone runs a shop or a company, use "at drive" (to run) instead: "Hun driver en butik" (She runs a shop).

sentence.da: Hvilket parti vil **regere** landet efter valget?
sentence.en: Which party will govern the country after the election?

at registrere.explanation: "At registrere" means "to register". To say an official list adds people, say: "Kommunen registrerer alle borgere" (The municipality registers all citizens). To say you notice something, it also works: "Jeg registrerede ikke, at han gik" (I did not notice that he left).

sentence.da: Du skal **registrere** din bil, før du må køre i den.
sentence.en: You have to register your car before you may drive it.

at regne.explanation: "At regne" means "to rain". To say it is raining, say: "Det regner" (It is raining). To say someone does sums, it also means "to calculate": "Han regner hurtigt" (He calculates quickly).

sentence.da: I dag skal det **regne**.
sentence.en: Today it is going to rain.

at regne med.explanation: "At regne med" means "to count on or expect". To say you depend on a person, say: "Jeg regner med dig" (I am counting on you). To say you expect something, say: "Vi regner med regn i morgen" (We expect rain tomorrow).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **regne med** hjælp fra min bror.
sentence.en: I can count on help from my brother.

at rehabilitere.explanation: "At rehabilitere" means "to rehabilitate". The noun is "rehabilitering" (rehabilitation): "Efter operationen kom han i rehabilitering" (After the operation he went into rehabilitation). To say someone gets their good name back, use it too: "Han blev rehabiliteret efter sagen" (He was rehabilitated after the case).

sentence.da: Vi skal **rehabilitere** patienten, så han kan gå igen.
sentence.en: We must rehabilitate the patient so that he can walk again.

at rejse.explanation: "At rejse" means "to travel". To say you are leaving, say: "Jeg rejser i morgen" (I am leaving tomorrow). The noun is "en rejse" (a trip): "Vi tog på en lang rejse" (We went on a long trip).

sentence.da: Vi vil **rejse** til Spanien i morgen.
sentence.en: We want to travel to Spain tomorrow.

at rejse sig.explanation: "At rejse sig" means "to stand up or rise". The small word "sig" (oneself) must come after it and changes with the person. To say who stands up, use "mig" (myself) for "I" and "dig" (yourself) for "you": "Jeg rejser mig" (I stand up), "Du rejser dig" (You stand up).

sentence.da: Alle skal **rejse sig**, når læreren kommer ind.
sentence.en: Everyone has to stand up when the teacher comes in.

at rekruttere.explanation: "At rekruttere" means "to recruit". It comes from "en rekrut" (a recruit). To say a company looks for staff, say: "Vi rekrutterer nye kolleger" (We are recruiting new colleagues).

sentence.da: Firmaet vil **rekruttere** ti nye medarbejdere i år.
sentence.en: The company wants to recruit ten new employees this year.

at renovere.explanation: "At renovere" means "to renovate". To say you only paint a room, use "at male" (to paint) instead: "Vi maler stuen" (We are painting the living room). The noun is "en renovering" (a renovation): "Renoveringen tager to måneder" (The renovation takes two months).

sentence.da: Vi vil **renovere** badeværelset, fordi fliserne er gamle.
sentence.en: We want to renovate the bathroom because the tiles are old.

at rense.explanation: "At rense" means "to clean", as in taking dirt out of something. To say you clean water, say: "Vi renser vandet" (We clean the water). To say you clean a house, use "at gøre rent" (to clean) instead: "Jeg gør rent" (I clean the house).

sentence.da: Du skal **rense** såret med vand.
sentence.en: You have to clean the wound with water.

at reparere.explanation: "At reparere" means "to repair". To say the opposite, use "at ødelægge" (to ruin): "Han ødelagde min cykel" (He ruined my bike).

sentence.da: Kan du **reparere** min cykel i dag?
sentence.en: Can you repair my bike today?

at repetere.explanation: "At repetere" means "to review", as in going over what you have studied. To say you study before a test, say: "Jeg repeterer til prøven" (I am reviewing for the test). To say something again, use "at gentage" (to repeat) instead: "Kan du gentage det?" (Can you repeat that?)

sentence.da: Før prøven skal jeg **repetere** alle ordene fra i år.
sentence.en: Before the test I have to review all the words from this year.

at repræsentere.explanation: "At repræsentere" means "to represent". To say you speak or act for a country, say: "Hun repræsenterer Danmark ved OL" (She represents Denmark at the Olympics). To say a symbol stands for an idea, say: "Flaget repræsenterer frihed" (The flag stands for freedom).

sentence.da: Han skal **repræsentere** hele klassen ved mødet i morgen.
sentence.en: He is going to represent the whole class at the meeting tomorrow.

at reservere.explanation: "At reservere" means "to reserve". To say you book a table, Danes also use "at booke" (to book): "Jeg har booket et bord" (I have booked a table).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **reservere** et bord i aften.
sentence.en: I would like to reserve a table tonight.

at respektere.explanation: "At respektere" means "to respect". The noun is "respekt" (respect), used with "for" (for): "Jeg har stor respekt for hende" (I have great respect for her).

sentence.da: Du skal **respektere** andre menneskers valg.
sentence.en: You have to respect other people's choices.

at respondere.explanation: "At respondere" means "to respond". To say a machine gives no answer, say: "Appen responderer ikke" (The app is not responding). To say a person answers a message, use "at svare" (to answer) instead: "Hun svarede på mailen" (She answered the email).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **respondere**, før jeg har læst mailen.
sentence.en: I cannot respond before I have read the email.

at restaurere.explanation: "At restaurere" means "to restore". To say an old building was put back as it was, say: "Kirken er blevet restaureret" (The church has been restored). For a computer file, use "at gendanne" (to bring back) instead: "Jeg gendanner filen" (I restore the file).

sentence.da: Han bruger mange år på at **restaurere** gamle møbler.
sentence.en: He spends many years restoring old furniture.

at retfærdiggøre.explanation: "At retfærdiggøre" means "to justify". It is built from "retfærdig" (fair) and "at gøre" (to make). To say that nothing makes something acceptable, say: "Intet kan retfærdiggøre vold" (Nothing can justify violence).

sentence.da: Han prøver at **retfærdiggøre** sit valg, men ingen tror på ham.
sentence.en: He tries to justify his choice, but nobody believes him.

at rette.explanation: "At rette" means "to correct or straighten". To say you fix a mistake, say: "Kan du rette fejlen i teksten?" (Can you correct the mistake in the text?) To say you make your body straight, say: "Hun rettede ryggen" (She straightened her back).

sentence.da: Læreren skal **rette** vores prøver i aften.
sentence.en: The teacher has to correct our tests tonight.

at returnere.explanation: "At returnere" means "to return an item". To say a person comes back, use "at vende tilbage" (to come back) instead: "Hun vender tilbage i morgen" (She comes back tomorrow).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **returnere** jakken, fordi den er for stor.
sentence.en: I want to return the jacket because it is too big.

at ride.explanation: "At ride" means "to ride (a horse)". To say someone rides regularly, say: "Hun rider hver weekend" (She rides every weekend). To say you ride a bike, use "at cykle" (to cycle) instead: "Jeg cykler på arbejde" (I cycle to work).

sentence.da: Hun kan **ride** på hesten i skoven.
sentence.en: She can ride the horse in the forest.

at ringe.explanation: "At ringe" means "to call", as in on the phone. To say who you call, add "til" (to) before the person: "Jeg ringer til dig i morgen" (I will call you tomorrow). To say a bell makes its sound, it means "to ring": "Klokken ringer" (The bell is ringing).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **ringe** til min mor.
sentence.en: I want to call my mother.

at ringe efter.explanation: "At ringe efter" means "to call for". To say you phone for someone to come, say: "Vi ringer efter en taxa" (We call a taxi). To phone a person, use "at ringe til" instead: "Jeg ringer til Anna" (I call Anna).

sentence.da: Vi må **ringe efter** en læge nu.
sentence.en: We have to call for a doctor now.

at ringe op.explanation: "At ringe op" means "to call", as in on the phone. To say you call someone, put the person between "ringe" and "op": "Jeg ringer dig op" (I call you). "At ringe til" means the same: "Jeg ringer til dig" (I call you).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **ringe op** og bestille en pizza.
sentence.en: I want to call and order a pizza.

at ringe på.explanation: "At ringe på" means "to ring the doorbell". To say someone is at the door, say: "Der ringer nogen på" (Someone is ringing the doorbell). To phone someone, use "at ringe til" instead: "Jeg ringer til dig" (I call you).

sentence.da: Du kan **ringe på**, hvis døren er låst.
sentence.en: You can ring the doorbell if the door is locked.

at ringe til.explanation: "At ringe til" means "to call", as in on the phone. The word "til" (to) comes right before the person: "Jeg ringer til min far" (I call my father). To say a bell makes its sound, use "at ringe" without "til": "Klokken ringer" (The bell is ringing).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **ringe til** min mor.
sentence.en: I want to call my mother.

at ringe tilbage.explanation: "At ringe tilbage" means "to call back". The word "tilbage" (back) is also in "at komme tilbage" (to come back) and "at give tilbage" (to give back).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **ringe tilbage**, når jeg er hjemme.
sentence.en: I will call back when I am home.

at risikere.explanation: "At risikere" means "to risk". It comes from "en risiko" (a risk). To say a bad result may follow, say: "Du risikerer en bøde, hvis du parkerer her" (You risk a fine if you park here).

sentence.da: Du kan **risikere** at komme for sent.
sentence.en: You might end up being late.

at riste.explanation: "At riste" means "to toast or roast". To say you toast bread, say: "Jeg rister brødet" (I toast the bread). Do not mix it up with "at ryste" (to shake): "Jeg ryster flasken" (I shake the bottle).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **riste** nødderne på en tør pande.
sentence.en: I want to toast the nuts in a dry pan.

at rive.explanation: "At rive" means "to grate". To say you grate vegetables, say: "Jeg river gulerødderne" (I grate the carrots). To say you rake leaves, it also means "to rake": "Han river bladene sammen" (He rakes the leaves together).

sentence.da: Jeg skal **rive** ost til pastaen.
sentence.en: I have to grate cheese for the pasta.

at rive i stykker.explanation: "At rive i stykker" means "to tear to pieces". To say a child tears paper, say: "Barnet river papiret i stykker" (The child tears the paper to pieces). The words "i stykker" (in pieces) are also in "at skære i stykker" (to cut into pieces) and "at falde i stykker" (to fall apart).

sentence.da: Hunden plejer at **rive i stykker** gamle sko.
sentence.en: The dog usually tears old shoes to pieces.

at rive ned.explanation: "At rive ned" means "to tear down". To say a building is demolished, say: "De river det gamle hus ned" (They are tearing down the old house). To say "it" instead of the building, put "det" before "ned": "De river det ned" (They are tearing it down).

sentence.da: De vil **rive ned** det gamle hus.
sentence.en: They want to tear down the old house.

at ro.explanation: "At ro" means "to row". To say someone rows regularly, say: "Hun roer hver morgen" (She rows every morning). Do not mix it up with the noun "ro", which means "calm": "Jeg vil have lidt ro" (I want some peace and quiet).

sentence.da: Vi kan **ro** over søen i en lille båd.
sentence.en: We can row across the lake in a small boat.

at rode.explanation: "At rode" means "to rummage or mess up". To say you search through things for something, add "efter" (for): "Han roder efter sine briller" (He is rummaging for his glasses). To say a place was left untidy, say: "Børnene har rodet i stuen" (The children have made a mess in the living room).

sentence.da: Han må **rode** i tasken for at finde sine nøgler.
sentence.en: He has to rummage in the bag to find his keys.

at rose.explanation: "At rose" means "to praise". To say someone received praise, say: "Hun blev rost af chefen" (She was praised by the boss). Do not mix it up with "en rose" (a rose): "Hun har en rose" (She has a rose).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **rose** dig for dit arbejde.
sentence.en: I want to praise you for your work.

at rulle.explanation: "At rulle" means "to roll". To say something moves by turning over and over, say: "Bilen ruller langsomt" (The car rolls slowly). To say you roll something yourself, say: "Jeg ruller dejen" (I roll the dough).

sentence.da: Bolden kan **rulle** ned ad bakken.
sentence.en: The ball can roll down the hill.

at runde af.explanation: "At runde af" means "to round off". To say you round a number, say: "Jeg runder 4,6 af til 5" (I round 4.6 off to 5). To say you finish an event, say: "Vi rundede aftenen af med kaffe" (We rounded off the evening with coffee).

sentence.da: Vi vil **runde af** med en kop kaffe.
sentence.en: We want to round off with a cup of coffee.

at runde ned.explanation: "At runde ned" means "to round down". To say you lower a number, say: "Hun runder 7,4 ned til 7" (She rounds 7.4 down to 7). The word "ned" (down) is also in "at skrive ned" (to write down).

sentence.da: Prisen er 52 kroner, men vi kan **runde ned** til 50.
sentence.en: The price is 52 kroner, but we can round down to 50.

at runde op.explanation: "At runde op" means "to round up". To say you raise a number, say: "Vi runder 7,6 op til 8" (We round 7.6 up to 8). To lower a number instead, use "at runde ned" (to round down): "Vi runder 7,4 ned til 7" (We round 7.4 down to 7). The word "op" (up) is also in "at tage op" (to pick up).

sentence.da: Du kan **runde op** til nærmeste hundrede.
sentence.en: You can round up to the nearest hundred.

at rydde.explanation: "At rydde" means "to clear". To say you clear something away, say: "Han rydder sneen væk" (He clears the snow away). To say you tidy up, add "op" (up): "Børnene rydder op" (The children tidy up).

sentence.da: Efter maden skal vi **rydde** bordet.
sentence.en: After the meal we have to clear the table.

at rydde op.explanation: "At rydde op" means "to tidy up". It is built from "at rydde" (to clear) and "op" (up). To say what you tidy, add "i" (in): "Jeg rydder op i stuen" (I tidy up the living room).

sentence.da: Du skal **rydde op** på dit værelse nu.
sentence.en: You have to tidy up your room now.

at ryge.explanation: "At ryge" means "to smoke". To say you do not smoke, say: "Jeg ryger ikke" (I do not smoke). To name the smoke itself, use "røg": "Der er røg i køkkenet" (There is smoke in the kitchen).

sentence.da: Han vil gerne holde op med at **ryge**.
sentence.en: He would like to quit smoking.

at rykke.explanation: "At rykke" means "to move or pull". To say people shift a short way, say: "Vi rykker tættere sammen" (We move closer together). To say someone gives a quick tug, add "i" (at): "Hun rykkede i snoren" (She tugged the cord).

sentence.da: Kan I **rykke** lidt, så der er plads til mig?
sentence.en: Can you move over a bit so there is room for me?

at rynke.explanation: "At rynke" means "to wrinkle or frown". To say paper gets small lines, say: "Papiret rynker, når det bliver vådt" (The paper wrinkles when it gets wet). To say someone frowns, use "panden" (the forehead): "Hun rynkede panden" (She frowned; literally, "She wrinkled the forehead").

sentence.da: Skjorten vil **rynke**, hvis du propper den ned i kufferten.
sentence.en: The shirt will wrinkle if you stuff it into the suitcase.

at ryste.explanation: "At ryste" means "to shake". To say someone trembles, add "af" (from) and the cause: "Hun ryster af kulde" (She is shaking from the cold).

sentence.da: Du skal **ryste** flasken før brug.
sentence.en: You have to shake the bottle before use.

at ryste på hovedet.explanation: "At ryste på hovedet" means "to shake one's head". It is built from "at ryste" (to shake) and "hovedet" (the head). To name what you shook your head at, add "ad" (at) before it: "Jeg rystede på hovedet ad hans svar" (I shook my head at his answer).

sentence.da: Hun kunne kun **ryste på hovedet**, da hun hørte prisen.
sentence.en: She could only shake her head when she heard the price.

at råbe.explanation: "At råbe" means "to shout". To shout at a person, add "ad" (at): "Han råber ad mig" (He is yelling at me). To call out for something, use "på" (for): "Jeg råbte på hjælp" (I shouted for help).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **råbe** så højt herinde.
sentence.en: You must not shout so loudly in here.

at råde over.explanation: "At råde over" means "to have at one's disposal". Without "over", the verb "at råde" means "to advise": "Jeg råder dig til at vente" (I advise you to wait).

forms.en: I have had at my disposal

sentence.da: Skolen kan **råde over** en stor sal til festen.
sentence.en: The school can have a big hall at its disposal for the party.

at rådføre sig.explanation: "At rådføre sig" means "to consult". To name the person you consult, add "med" (with) before that person. After "jeg" (I), "sig" (oneself) becomes "mig" (myself): "Jeg rådfører mig med lægen" (I consult the doctor).

sentence.da: Hun vil **rådføre sig** med en advokat og læse kontrakten først.
sentence.en: She will consult a lawyer and read the contract first.

at rådne.explanation: "At rådne" means "to rot". The word for "rotten" is "rådden": "en rådden banan" (a rotten banana).

sentence.da: Træet vil **rådne**, hvis det står ude i regnen hele vinteren.
sentence.en: The wood will rot if it stands outside in the rain all winter.

at række.explanation: "At række" means "to reach or hand". When you pass something to someone, say: "Kan du række mig saltet?" (Can you hand me the salt?). When you say there is enough of something, say: "Pengene rækker ikke" (The money is not enough).

sentence.da: Kan du **række** mig en kop, tak?
sentence.en: Can you hand me a cup, please?

at række hånden op.explanation: "At række hånden op" means "to raise one's hand". To say it is your own hand, Danish says "hånden" (the hand), not "min hånd" (my hand): "Hun rakte hånden op" (She raised her hand).

sentence.da: Hun vil **række hånden op**, når hun kender svaret.
sentence.en: She wants to raise her hand when she knows the answer.

at rødme.explanation: "At rødme" means "to blush". It is built from "rød" (red). To say someone is red in the face from effort, use "rød i hovedet" (red in the face): "Han er rød i hovedet efter løbeturen" (He is red in the face after the run).

sentence.da: Han plejer at **rødme**, når nogen roser ham foran andre.
sentence.en: He usually blushes when someone praises him in front of others.

at røre.explanation: "At røre" means "to touch or stir". To say you stir food, say: "Rør i suppen" (Stir the soup). To say you touch something, add "ved" after the verb: "Rør ikke ved min telefon" (Do not touch my phone).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **røre** ved ovnen, fordi den er varm.
sentence.en: You must not touch the oven, because it is hot.

at røre rundt.explanation: "At røre rundt" means "to stir". "Rundt" means "around", and it also works with other verbs: "at gå rundt" (to walk around), "at køre rundt" (to drive around).

sentence.da: Du skal **røre rundt** i gryden hele tiden.
sentence.en: You have to stir the pot all the time.

at røve.explanation: "At røve" means "to rob". To say someone takes something without threatening anyone, use "at stjæle" (to steal): "Nogen har stjålet min cykel" (Someone has stolen my bike).

sentence.da: Tre mænd prøvede at **røve** banken, men blev fanget.
sentence.en: Three men tried to rob the bank but were caught.

en rabat.explanation: "En rabat" means "a discount". To ask for a discount, leave out "en": "Kan jeg få rabat?" (Can I get a discount?).

sentence.da: Butikken giver mig **rabat** på en jakke.
sentence.en: The store gives me a discount on a jacket.

en race.explanation: "En race" means "a breed". To say a dog breed, join "hund" (dog) and "race": "en hunderace" (a dog breed). To say a running race, use "et løb" (a race): "Hun vandt løbet" (She won the race).

sentence.da: Labrador er en **race**, som mange bruger som førerhund.
sentence.en: Labrador is a breed that many use as a guide dog.

en radar.explanation: "En radar" means "a radar". To say something shows up on it, use "på radaren" (on the radar): "Flyet er på radaren" (The plane is on the radar).

sentence.da: Skibet kan se andre skibe på sin **radar**.
sentence.en: The ship can see other ships on its radar.

en radiator.explanation: "En radiator" means "a radiator". To say you turn up the heat, say: "Jeg skruer op for radiatoren" (I turn up the radiator).

sentence.da: Der er en **radiator** under vinduet, og den er varm.
sentence.en: There is a radiator under the window, and it is warm.

en radio.explanation: "En radio" means "a radio". To say something was on the radio, Danish says "i radioen" (literally, "in the radio"): "Det var i radioen" (It was on the radio).

sentence.da: Jeg hører **radio** og musik i bilen.
sentence.en: I listen to the radio and music in the car.

en radioavis.explanation: "En radioavis" means "a radio news broadcast". It is built from "radio" (radio) and "avis" (newspaper). To say you read the printed paper, use "avis" alone: "Jeg læser avisen" (I read the newspaper).

sentence.da: I en **radioavis** hører man nyheder.
sentence.en: In a radio news broadcast you hear the news.

en radius.explanation: "En radius" means "a radius". To say within a distance of a place, use "inden for en radius af" (within a radius of): "Alle butikker inden for en radius af to kilometer" (All shops within a radius of two kilometers).

sentence.da: Hvis **radius** er fem centimeter, er cirklen ti centimeter bred.
sentence.en: If the radius is five centimeters, the circle is ten centimeters wide.

en raket.explanation: "En raket" means "a rocket". When you talk about a firework that shoots into the sky, you also use "raket": "Han tændte en raket" (He lit a rocket).

sentence.da: En **raket** bruger brændstof til at flyve helt op i rummet.
sentence.en: A rocket uses fuel to fly all the way up into space.

en rang.explanation: "En rang" means "a rank". To describe a person of high standing, say: "en mand af høj rang" (a man of high rank).

sentence.da: Soldaten fik en højere **rang**, efter at han havde reddet holdet.
sentence.en: The soldier got a higher rank after he had saved the team.

en rangorden.explanation: "En rangorden" means "a ranking". It is built from "rang" (rank) and "orden" (order). To say a group of animals or people has a pecking order, use "en hakkeorden" (a pecking order): "Der er en hakkeorden blandt kollegerne" (There is a pecking order among the colleagues).

sentence.da: Hos hønsene er der en fast **rangorden**.
sentence.en: Among the hens there is a fixed ranking.

en rapport.explanation: "En rapport" means "a report". To say you write one, use "at skrive" (to write): "Jeg skriver en rapport" (I am writing a report).

sentence.da: Jeg skal aflevere min **rapport** i morgen.
sentence.en: I have to hand in my report tomorrow.

en reaktion.explanation: "En reaktion" means "a reaction". To say what a reaction is about, use "på" (to): "en reaktion på nyheden" (a reaction to the news).

sentence.da: Hans **reaktion** var meget rolig.
sentence.en: His reaction was very calm.

en recept.explanation: "En recept" means "a prescription". For a cooking recipe, use "en opskrift" (a recipe): "Jeg har en opskrift på kage" (I have a recipe for cake).

sentence.da: Lægen giver mig en **recept** til apoteket.
sentence.en: The doctor gives me a prescription for the pharmacy.

en reception.explanation: "En reception" means "a reception desk". It also means a party where guests are received: "Vi holder reception på fredag" (We are holding a reception on Friday).

sentence.da: Hotellet har en **reception**, og den er åben hele natten.
sentence.en: The hotel has a front desk, and it is open all night.

en receptionist.explanation: "En receptionist" means "a receptionist". It is built from "reception" (reception desk) and the ending "-ist", as in "en pianist" (a pianist).

sentence.da: På hotellet hjælper en **receptionist** gæsterne med at tjekke ind.
sentence.en: At the hotel a receptionist helps the guests check in.

en recession.explanation: "En recession" means "a recession". To say a country is in one, leave out "en": "Landet er i recession" (The country is in a recession).

sentence.da: Under en **recession** køber folk mindre, så flere firmaer lukker.
sentence.en: During a recession people buy less, so more firms close.

en redaktion.explanation: "En redaktion" means "an editorial office". To say where someone works, use "på" (at): "Hun arbejder på redaktionen" (She works at the editorial office).

sentence.da: På en **redaktion** skriver og vælger man nyheder til avisen.
sentence.en: At an editorial office, people write and choose the news for the paper.

en redaktør.explanation: "En redaktør" means "an editor". To say the editor in charge, add "chef" (boss) in front: "en chefredaktør" (an editor in chief).

sentence.da: Hun er **redaktør** og læser alle artikler, før de udkommer.
sentence.en: She is an editor and reads all articles before they come out.

en rede.explanation: "En rede" means "a nest". To say a bird makes its nest, use "at bygge rede" (to build a nest): "Fuglene bygger rede i træet" (The birds are building a nest in the tree).

sentence.da: Fuglen har lagt tre æg i sin **rede**.
sentence.en: The bird has laid three eggs in its nest.

en redegørelse.explanation: "En redegørelse" means "an account or report". To ask someone to explain what happened, say: "Jeg vil have en redegørelse for, hvad der skete" (I want an account of what happened). It comes from the verb "at redegøre for" (to account for).

sentence.da: Direktøren skrev en **redegørelse** om ulykken.
sentence.en: The director wrote a report about the accident.

en redning.explanation: "En redning" means "a rescue". It comes from the verb "at redde" (to save).

sentence.da: Politiets **redning** af drengen fra isen tog en time.
sentence.en: The police's rescue of the boy from the ice took an hour.

en redningskrans.explanation: "En redningskrans" means "a lifebuoy". It is built from "redning" (rescue) and "krans" (wreath), as in "en julekrans" (a Christmas wreath).

sentence.da: Han kastede en **redningskrans** ud til manden i vandet.
sentence.en: He threw a lifebuoy out to the man in the water.

en redningsvest.explanation: "En redningsvest" means "a life jacket". It is built from "redning" (rescue) and "vest" (vest). "Vest" also means "west": "Vi kører mod vest" (We drive west).

sentence.da: Alle børn skal have **redningsvest** på i båden.
sentence.en: All children must wear a life jacket in the boat.

en reform.explanation: "En reform" means "a reform". To say a reform of schools, join "skole" (school) and "reform": "en skolereform" (a school reform).

sentence.da: Politikerne vil gøre skolen bedre med en stor **reform**.
sentence.en: The politicians want to make school better with a big reform.

en regel.explanation: "En regel" means "a rule". A very common phrase is "som regel" (as a rule): "Som regel venter jeg" (As a rule, I wait).

sentence.da: Der er en **regel** om at vente her.
sentence.en: There is a rule about waiting here.

en regering.explanation: "En regering" means "a government". To say politicians form a new government, use "at danne regering" (to form a government), with no "en": "De vil danne regering" (They want to form a government).

sentence.da: Den nye **regering** vil bygge flere skoler.
sentence.en: The new government wants to build more schools.

en region.explanation: "En region" means "a region". In Denmark, there are five regions, and they run the hospitals.

sentence.da: Hver **region** i Danmark har sine egne sygehuse.
sentence.en: Each region in Denmark has its own hospitals.

en regnbue.explanation: "En regnbue" means "a rainbow". It is built from "regn" (rain) and "bue" (arc). "Bue" also means "bow", as in "pil og bue" (bow and arrow).

sentence.da: Solen og regnen laver en **regnbue** på himlen.
sentence.en: The sun and the rain make a rainbow in the sky.

en regnbyge.explanation: "En regnbyge" means "a rain shower". It is built from "regn" (rain) and "byge" (shower). "Byge" is also in "en snebyge" (a snow shower).

sentence.da: Vi blev våde i en kort **regnbyge**.
sentence.en: We got wet in a short rain shower.

en regning.explanation: "En regning" means "a bill". To ask for the bill in a restaurant, say: "Må jeg bede om regningen?" (May I ask for the bill?).

sentence.da: Jeg betaler en **regning** for strøm.
sentence.en: I pay a bill for electricity.

en regnjakke.explanation: "En regnjakke" means "a rain jacket". It is built from "regn" (rain) and "jakke" (jacket). The same "regn" is in "en regnbue" (a rainbow).

sentence.da: Jeg tager min **regnjakke** på i regnen.
sentence.en: I put my rain jacket on in the rain.

en regnskov.explanation: "En regnskov" means "a rainforest". It is built from "regn" (rain) and "skov" (forest). To say it must be protected, say: "Vi skal redde regnskoven" (We must save the rainforest).

sentence.da: Det regner hele året i en **regnskov**.
sentence.en: It rains all year in a rainforest.

en regnvejrsdag.explanation: "En regnvejrsdag" means "a rainy day". It is built from "regnvejr" (rainy weather) and "dag" (day). To say you save money for hard times, say: "Jeg sparer op til en regnvejrsdag" (I am saving up for a rainy day).

sentence.da: Det regner i dag, og det er en rigtig **regnvejrsdag**.
sentence.en: It is raining today, and it is a real rainy day.

en regulering.explanation: "En regulering" means "a regulation or adjustment". When you set something to the right level, say: "en regulering af varmen" (an adjustment of the heat). When the authorities set official limits, say: "en regulering af priserne" (a regulation of prices).

sentence.da: Staten har indført en **regulering** af huslejen.
sentence.en: The state has introduced a regulation of rents.

en reje.explanation: "En reje" means "a shrimp". Put on bread, it makes "en rejemad" (a shrimp open sandwich).

sentence.da: En **reje** er et lille dyr i havet.
sentence.en: A shrimp is a small animal in the sea.

en rejemad.explanation: "En rejemad" means "a shrimp open sandwich". It is built from "reje" (shrimp) and "mad". "Mad" means "food", but at the end of a word like this it means a slice of bread with a topping, as in "en ostemad" (a cheese sandwich).

sentence.da: En **rejemad** er brød med rejer, mayonnaise og citron.
sentence.en: A shrimp open sandwich is bread with shrimp, mayonnaise and lemon.

en rejse.explanation: "En rejse" means "a trip or a journey". For a short outing, use "en tur" (a trip, a walk): "en tur i skoven" (a walk in the forest). To wish someone a good journey, say: "God rejse!" (Have a good trip!).

sentence.da: Vi tager på en lang **rejse** til Spanien.
sentence.en: We are going on a long trip to Spain.

en rejseforsikring.explanation: "En rejseforsikring" means "a travel insurance policy". It is built from "rejse" (trip) and "forsikring" (insurance).

sentence.da: Hvis jeg bliver syg, betaler min **rejseforsikring**.
sentence.en: If I get sick, my travel insurance pays.

en rejsende.explanation: "En rejsende" means "a traveler". It comes from "at rejse" (to travel). The ending "-ende" turns a verb into a person, as in "en studerende" (a student).

sentence.da: Alle **rejsende** skal vise deres pas.
sentence.en: All travelers have to show their passports.

en rejseplan.explanation: "En rejseplan" means "an itinerary". "Rejseplanen" is also the name of the Danish app and website for planning bus and train journeys. For a bus or train timetable, use "en køreplan" (a timetable): "Jeg læser køreplanen" (I am reading the timetable).

sentence.da: Min **rejseplan** viser hotellet og flyet.
sentence.en: My itinerary shows the hotel and the flight.

en reklamation.explanation: "En reklamation" means "a complaint (faulty item)". The matching verb is "at reklamere" (to make a claim): "Jeg vil reklamere over telefonen" (I want to complain about the phone).

sentence.da: Jeg skriver en **reklamation**, fordi telefonen er gået i stykker.
sentence.en: I am writing a complaint because the phone has broken.

en reklame.explanation: "En reklame" means "an advertisement". To say you advertise something, use "at gøre reklame for" (to advertise): "De gør reklame for en ny bil" (They are advertising a new car). It also means "a commercial" on TV: "Jeg hader reklamer i fjernsynet" (I hate commercials on TV).

sentence.da: Der var en lang **reklame** midt i filmen.
sentence.en: There was a long commercial in the middle of the movie.

en rekord.explanation: "En rekord" means "a record". To say someone beats the best result, use "at slå" (to beat): "Hun slog rekorden" (She broke the record). A music record is "en plade" (a record): "Jeg har mange plader" (I have many records).

sentence.da: Hun satte ny **rekord** i svømning i går.
sentence.en: She set a new record in swimming yesterday.

en rektor.explanation: "En rektor" means "a principal". The head of a university is also called "rektor": "Universitetets rektor holdt en tale" (The university's rector gave a speech).

sentence.da: Skolens **rektor** er chef for alle lærerne.
sentence.en: The school's principal is the boss of all the teachers.

en religion.explanation: "En religion" means "a religion". The matching adjective is "religiøs" (religious): "en religiøs person" (a religious person).

sentence.da: Kristendom er en **religion**, og islam er en anden.
sentence.en: Christianity is a religion, and Islam is another.

en ren.explanation: "En ren" means "a reindeer". The same spelling without "en" is the adjective "ren" (clean): "Vandet er rent" (The water is clean).

sentence.da: En **ren** har store gevirer og lever i det kolde nord.
sentence.en: A reindeer has big antlers and lives in the cold north.

en rengøring.explanation: "En rengøring" means "a cleaning". For housecleaning in general, leave out "en": "Rengøring tager lang tid" (Cleaning takes a long time). It comes from the verb "at rengøre" (to clean).

sentence.da: Jeg hader **rengøring**, men huset skal være rent.
sentence.en: I hate cleaning, but the house has to be clean.

en rengøringsassistent.explanation: "En rengøringsassistent" means "a cleaner". It is built from "rengøring" (cleaning) and "assistent" (assistant).

sentence.da: En **rengøringsassistent** gør kontorerne rene hver aften.
sentence.en: A cleaner cleans the offices every evening.

en renovering.explanation: "En renovering" means "a renovation". The verb is "at renovere" (to renovate): "Vi renoverer køkkenet" (We are renovating the kitchen).

sentence.da: Huset fik nyt tag og nye vinduer ved en **renovering**.
sentence.en: The house got a new roof and new windows in a renovation.

en rente.explanation: "En rente" means "an interest rate". To talk about interest in general, leave out "en": "at betale rente" (to pay interest).

sentence.da: Banken tager en høj **rente**, når man låner penge.
sentence.en: The bank charges a high interest rate when you borrow money.

en rentestigning.explanation: "En rentestigning" means "an interest rate rise". It is built from "rente" (interest) and "stigning" (a rise), the same pattern as "en prisstigning" (a price rise).

sentence.da: En **rentestigning** gør det dyrere at betale sit lån tilbage.
sentence.en: An interest rate rise makes it more expensive to pay your loan back.

en reol.explanation: "En reol" means "a bookshelf". A single shelf is "en hylde" (a shelf): "Bogen ligger på hylden" (The book is on the shelf).

sentence.da: Der står mange bøger i min **reol**.
sentence.en: There are many books on my bookshelf.

en reparation.explanation: "En reparation" means "a repair". The matching verb is "at reparere" (to repair): "Jeg skal reparere cyklen" (I have to repair the bike).

sentence.da: Der er brug for en **reparation** af taget.
sentence.en: The roof needs a repair.

en replik.explanation: "En replik" means "a line or retort". To ask about an actor's line in a play, say: "Hvad er min næste replik?" (What is my next line?). To describe a quick comeback in an argument, say: "Det var en skarp replik" (That was a sharp retort).

sentence.da: På scenen skal skuespilleren huske sin **replik**.
sentence.en: On stage, the actor has to remember his line.

en repræsentant.explanation: "En repræsentant" means "a representative". To say who the representative stands for, add "for" (of): "en repræsentant for firmaet" (a representative of the company).

sentence.da: Hver klasse vælger en **repræsentant** til elevrådet.
sentence.en: Each class chooses a representative for the student council.

en reservation.explanation: "En reservation" means "a reservation". To say you book a table, use "at bestille bord" (to book a table): "Jeg vil gerne bestille bord til to" (I would like to book a table for two).

sentence.da: Vi har en **reservation** på restauranten i aften.
sentence.en: We have a reservation at the restaurant tonight.

en reservedel.explanation: "En reservedel" means "a spare part". It is built from "reserve" (spare) and "del" (part).

sentence.da: Når cyklen går i stykker, skal jeg købe en **reservedel**.
sentence.en: When the bike breaks, I have to buy a spare part.

en ressource.explanation: "En ressource" means "a resource". A very common phrase is "naturlige ressourcer" (natural resources): "Vi må spare på de naturlige ressourcer" (We must save the natural resources).

sentence.da: Vand er en vigtig **ressource**, som vi skal passe på.
sentence.en: Water is an important resource that we must take care of.

en rest.explanation: "En rest" means "a remainder or a leftover". To say you rest, use "at hvile sig" (to rest): "Jeg hviler mig lidt" (I am resting a bit).

sentence.da: Der er en **rest** pizza i køleskabet.
sentence.en: There is some leftover pizza in the fridge.

en restaurant.explanation: "En restaurant" means "a restaurant". To say you go out to eat, use "at gå på restaurant" (to go to a restaurant), with no "en": "Skal vi gå på restaurant?" (Shall we go to a restaurant?).

sentence.da: Vi spiser på **restaurant** i aften.
sentence.en: We are eating at a restaurant tonight.

en restaurantgæst.explanation: "En restaurantgæst" means "a restaurant guest". The part "gæst" (guest) works in other words too: "en hotelgæst" (a hotel guest).

sentence.da: En **restaurantgæst** bestiller mad og betaler bagefter.
sentence.en: A restaurant guest orders food and pays afterwards.

en ret.explanation: "En ret" means "a right or a dish". When you talk about what you are allowed to have, it means "a right": "Vi har ret til ferie" (We have a right to vacation). When you talk about food on a menu, it means "a dish": "Hvad er din yndlingsret?" (What is your favorite dish?). Without "en", "at have ret" means "to be right": "Du har ret" (You are right).

sentence.da: Dagens **ret** er fisk med kartofler.
sentence.en: Today's dish is fish with potatoes.

en retning.explanation: "En retning" means "a direction". To ask which way someone is going, say: "I hvilken retning går du?" (Which direction are you going?).

sentence.da: Bussen kører i den rigtige **retning**.
sentence.en: The bus is going in the right direction.

en retssag.explanation: "En retssag" means "a court case". It is built from "ret" (court) and "sag" (case). "Ret" also means "dish": "en hovedret" (a main course).

sentence.da: Ved en **retssag** afgør en dommer, hvem der har ret.
sentence.en: In a court case, a judge decides who is right.

en retsstat.explanation: "En retsstat" means "a state governed by law". It is built from "rets" (of law) and "stat" (state), as in "en velfærdsstat" (a welfare state).

sentence.da: I en **retsstat** gælder reglerne for alle, også for politikere.
sentence.en: In a state governed by law, the rules apply to everyone, including politicians.

en rettelse.explanation: "En rettelse" means "a correction". The verb is "at rette" (to correct). To say a teacher marks homework, say: "Læreren retter opgaverne" (The teacher marks the assignments).

sentence.da: Vi sender en **rettelse**, fordi der er en stavefejl i teksten.
sentence.en: We are sending a correction because there is a spelling mistake in the text.

en rettighed.explanation: "En rettighed" means "a right". To say you have a right to something, use "ret til" (right to): "Du har ret til ferie" (You have a right to vacation).

sentence.da: At gå i skole er en **rettighed** for alle børn.
sentence.en: Going to school is a right for all children.

en returbillet.explanation: "En returbillet" means "a round-trip ticket". It is built from "retur" (back) and "billet" (ticket).

sentence.da: Jeg køber en **returbillet** til Aarhus og hjem.
sentence.en: I buy a round-trip ticket to Aarhus and back home.

en returnering.explanation: "En returnering" means "a return". For going back to a place, use "at vende tilbage" (to go back): "Jeg vender tilbage i morgen" (I will be back tomorrow).

sentence.da: Ved **returnering** af varen får du pengene tilbage.
sentence.en: When you return the item, you get your money back.

en returret.explanation: "En returret" means "a right of return". It is built from "retur" (return) and "ret" (right).

sentence.da: Butikken giver os **returret** i tredive dage.
sentence.en: The shop gives us a right of return for thirty days.

en revisor.explanation: "En revisor" means "an auditor". The person who keeps the books day to day is "en bogholder" (a bookkeeper): "Bogholderen betaler regningerne" (The bookkeeper pays the bills).

sentence.da: Firmaets **revisor** gennemgår tallene hvert år.
sentence.en: The company's auditor goes through the numbers every year.

en revne.explanation: "En revne" means "a crack". A wider opening is "en sprække" (a gap): "Lyset kommer ind gennem en sprække" (The light comes in through a gap).

sentence.da: Glasset er ikke gået i stykker, men der er en **revne**.
sentence.en: The glass has not broken, but there is a crack.

en revolution.explanation: "En revolution" means "a revolution". The person who takes part is "en revolutionær" (a revolutionary): "Han var en revolutionær" (He was a revolutionary).

sentence.da: Folket startede en **revolution** mod kongen.
sentence.en: The people started a revolution against the king.

en revolver.explanation: "En revolver" means "a revolver". To say someone pulls one out, use "at trække" (to pull): "Han trak en revolver" (He pulled out a revolver).

sentence.da: Betjenten har en **revolver** i bæltet.
sentence.en: The officer has a revolver on his belt.

en ridder.explanation: "En ridder" means "a knight". It is also an honor in Denmark: "Ridder af Dannebrog" (Knight of the Dannebrog order).

sentence.da: I middelalderen red en **ridder** ud for at kæmpe for kongen.
sentence.en: In the Middle Ages, a knight rode out to fight for the king.

en ridse.explanation: "En ridse" means "a scratch". The matching verb is "at ridse" (to scratch): "Nogen har ridset bilen" (Someone has scratched the car).

sentence.da: Der er en **ridse** på bilens dør.
sentence.en: There is a scratch on the car door.

en ring.explanation: "En ring" means "a ring". The same spelling is also the command of "at ringe" (to call): "Ring til mig!" (Call me!)

sentence.da: Hun har en **ring** på fingeren.
sentence.en: She has a ring on her finger.

en risalamande.explanation: "En risalamande" means "a Danish rice pudding". It is eaten cold with whipped cream at Christmas. One whole almond is hidden in it, and the person who finds it wins a small gift. The name comes from the French "riz à l'amande" (rice with almond).

sentence.da: Til jul spiser vi **risalamande** med varm kirsebærsovs.
sentence.en: At Christmas, we eat risalamande with warm cherry sauce.

en risiko.explanation: "En risiko" means "a risk". To say you accept a risk, use "at tage en risiko" (to take a risk): "Jeg vil ikke tage en risiko" (I do not want to take a risk).

sentence.da: Der er en **risiko** for regn i morgen.
sentence.en: There is a risk of rain tomorrow.

en rive.explanation: "En rive" means "a rake". The verb "at rive" means "to grate": "Jeg river osten" (I am grating the cheese).

sentence.da: Jeg samler bladene med en **rive**.
sentence.en: I gather the leaves with a rake.

en robot.explanation: "En robot" means "a robot". It comes first in compounds, as in "en robotstøvsuger" (a robot vacuum cleaner).

sentence.da: Min **robot** støvsuger gulvet hver dag.
sentence.en: My robot vacuums the floor every day.

en robåd.explanation: "En robåd" means "a rowboat". It is built from "ro" (to row) and "båd" (boat).

sentence.da: Vi tager en **robåd** ud på søen.
sentence.en: We take a rowboat out on the lake.

en rod.explanation: "En rod" means "a root". To say a plant has taken root, use "at slå rod" (to take root): "Planten har slået rod" (The plant has taken root). The word "rod" in the sense of "mess" is a different word: "Der er rod i stuen" (The living room is a mess).

sentence.da: Hver plante har en **rod** under jorden.
sentence.en: Every plant has a root under the ground.

en rolle.explanation: "En rolle" means "a role". When you talk about an actor, it means a part in a play or film: "Hun spiller en rolle i et teaterstykke" (She plays a role in a play). When you talk about someone in a group, it means the part that person has: "Han har en vigtig rolle" (He has an important role).

sentence.da: Hun fik en stor **rolle** i filmen.
sentence.en: She got a big role in the movie.

en roman.explanation: "En roman" means "a novel". To name the kind of novel, put the kind in front: "en kriminalroman" (a crime novel).

sentence.da: Forfatteren har skrevet en **roman** om krigen.
sentence.en: The author has written a novel about the war.

en romkugle.explanation: "En romkugle" means "a rum ball". It is built from "rom" (rum) and "kugle" (ball).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser en **romkugle**, og den smager af rom.
sentence.en: I eat a rum ball and it tastes of rum.

en rose.explanation: "En rose" means "a rose". To say a bunch of them, say: "et bundt roser" (a bunch of roses).

sentence.da: En **rose** har torne og dufter godt.
sentence.en: A rose has thorns and smells good.

en rosin.explanation: "En rosin" means "a raisin". A fresh grape is "en vindrue" (a grape): "Børnene spiser vindruer" (The children eat grapes).

sentence.da: En **rosin** er lille, sød og tør.
sentence.en: A raisin is small, sweet and dry.

en rotte.explanation: "En rotte" means "a rat". For a smaller animal, use "en mus" (a mouse): "Der er en mus i køkkenet" (There is a mouse in the kitchen).

sentence.da: Katten jagter en **rotte** i laden.
sentence.en: The cat chases a rat in the barn.

en router.explanation: "En router" means "a router". To tell someone what to try when the internet stops working: "Prøv at genstarte routeren" (Try restarting the router).

sentence.da: Jeg skal købe en ny **router**, fordi internettet er langsomt.
sentence.en: I have to buy a new router because the internet is slow.

en rude.explanation: "En rude" means "a window pane". To talk about the whole window, not just the glass, use "et vindue" (a window): "Vinduet er åbent" (The window is open).

sentence.da: Bolden slog en **rude** i stykker.
sentence.en: The ball broke a window pane.

en rullepølse.explanation: "En rullepølse" means "a rolled pork sausage". It is built from "rulle" (roll) and "pølse" (sausage), but it is not cooked: it is spiced pork that is sliced thin and eaten cold on bread.

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have **rullepølse** på rugbrød.
sentence.en: I would like to have rolled pork sausage on rye bread.

en rulletrappe.explanation: "En rulletrappe" means "an escalator". It is built from "at rulle" (to roll) and "en trappe" (a staircase). The same "rulle" is in "en rullestol" (a wheelchair).

sentence.da: Vi tager en **rulletrappe** op til caféen.
sentence.en: We take an escalator up to the café.

en runde.explanation: "En runde" means "a round", as in one turn in a game. To say you take a short walk: "Vi går en runde i parken" (We take a stroll in the park). To say you buy drinks for everyone: "Jeg giver en runde" (I am buying a round).

sentence.da: Vi spiller lige en **runde** mere, og så går vi.
sentence.en: We play one more round, and then we leave.

en rundkørsel.explanation: "En rundkørsel" means "a roundabout". It is built from "rund" (round) and "kørsel" (driving). Danish traffic goes counterclockwise around it. To tell someone which way to leave it: "Tag anden afkørsel i rundkørslen" (Take the second exit at the roundabout).

sentence.da: Der er en stor **rundkørsel** ved stationen.
sentence.en: There is a big roundabout by the station.

en rundvisning.explanation: "En rundvisning" means "a guided tour". It is built from "rund" (round) and "visning" (a showing). To ask for one: "Kan vi få en rundvisning?" (Can we get a tour?)

sentence.da: Der er en **rundvisning** på slottet klokken to.
sentence.en: There is a guided tour of the castle at two o'clock.

en rune.explanation: "En rune" means "a rune". A stone with runes cut into it is "en runesten" (a rune stone).

sentence.da: Hver **rune** på stenen er et tegn fra vikingetiden.
sentence.en: Each rune on the stone is a sign from the Viking Age.

en russer.explanation: "En russer" means "a Russian". It comes from "Rusland" (Russia). To say a person is Russian: "Min nabo er russer" (My neighbor is Russian). For the language, use "russisk" (Russian): "Hun taler russisk" (She speaks Russian).

sentence.da: Min kollega er **russer** og kommer fra Moskva.
sentence.en: My colleague is Russian and comes from Moscow.

en rute.explanation: "En rute" means "a route". To say where a bus goes: "Bussen kører på en fast rute gennem byen" (The bus runs on a fixed route through town).

sentence.da: Vi tager den korteste **rute** til byen.
sentence.en: We take the shortest route to town.

en rutine.explanation: "En rutine" means "a routine". It also means experience from doing something many times. To say someone is experienced: "Hun har stor rutine" (She has a lot of experience).

sentence.da: Jeg har en fast **rutine** hver morgen.
sentence.en: I have a fixed routine every morning.

en rutsjebane.explanation: "En rutsjebane" means "a slide or a roller coaster". To talk about the slide at a playground: "Børnene leger på rutsjebanen" (The children play on the slide). To talk about the ride at an amusement park: "Rutsjebanen i forlystelsesparken er hurtig" (The roller coaster at the amusement park is fast).

sentence.da: Hun glider ned ad en **rutsjebane** på legepladsen.
sentence.en: She slides down a slide at the playground.

en ryg.explanation: "En ryg" means "a back", as in the body part. To say your back hurts: "Jeg har ondt i ryggen" (My back hurts), literally "I have pain in the back". To say you lie face up: "Jeg ligger på ryggen" (I am lying on my back).

sentence.da: Han har en bred **ryg** og stærke skuldre.
sentence.en: He has a broad back and strong shoulders.

en rygrad.explanation: "En rygrad" means "a spine", as in the bones of the back. To say a person has courage, use "rygrad" the way English uses "backbone": "Hun har rygrad" (She has backbone).

sentence.da: Din **rygrad** går fra nakken og ned til bækkenet.
sentence.en: Your spine runs from the neck down to the pelvis.

en rygsæk.explanation: "En rygsæk" means "a backpack". It is built from "ryg" (back) and "sæk" (sack). To say you put it on: "Jeg tager rygsækken på" (I put on the backpack).

sentence.da: Jeg bærer min **rygsæk** på ryggen.
sentence.en: I carry my backpack on my back.

en rynke.explanation: "En rynke" means "a wrinkle". The same word is in a verb phrase. To say someone frowns: "Han rynker panden" (He frowns), literally "He wrinkles the forehead".

sentence.da: Hun har en dyb **rynke** mellem øjenbrynene.
sentence.en: She has a deep wrinkle between her eyebrows.

en rysten.explanation: "En rysten" means "a shiver". It comes from the verb "at ryste" (to shake). To say you shake from the cold: "Jeg ryster af kulde" (I am shaking from the cold).

sentence.da: Der gik en **rysten** gennem hele kroppen.
sentence.en: A shiver went through the whole body.

en rytme.explanation: "En rytme" means "a rhythm". To talk about the pattern of a day: "dagens rytme" (the rhythm of the day). To tell someone to keep the beat: "Hold rytmen" (Keep the rhythm).

sentence.da: Trommerne giver sangen en fast **rytme**.
sentence.en: The drums give the song a steady rhythm.

en rådgiver.explanation: "En rådgiver" means "an adviser". It is built from "råd" (advice) and "giver" (giver). To name a money adviser: "en økonomisk rådgiver" (a financial adviser).

sentence.da: Vores **rådgiver** i banken hjalp os med at vælge et lån.
sentence.en: Our adviser at the bank helped us choose a loan.

en række.explanation: "En række" means "a row". To talk about several rows: "rækker af stole" (rows of chairs). To say a number of things, use "en række" before the plural: "en række problemer" (a number of problems).

sentence.da: Vi sidder i første **række** i biografen.
sentence.en: We sit in the front row at the movie theater.

en rækkevidde.explanation: "En rækkevidde" means "a range or reach". It is built from "række" (reach) and "vidde" (width). To talk about how far an electric car can go: "elbilens rækkevidde" (the electric car's range). For something kept where children cannot get it: "uden for børns rækkevidde" (out of children's reach).

sentence.da: Radioen har en lang **rækkevidde** og virker næsten overalt.
sentence.en: The radio has a long range and works almost everywhere.

en ræv.explanation: "En ræv" means "a fox". To say someone is cunning: "Han er så snu som en ræv" (He is as sly as a fox).

sentence.da: Jeg så en **ræv** løbe over marken.
sentence.en: I saw a fox run across the field.

en rødbede.explanation: "En rødbede" means "a beet". The name starts with "rød" (red). To say pickled beets: "syltede rødbeder" (pickled beets).

sentence.da: Salaten er rød, fordi jeg har en **rødbede** i.
sentence.en: The salad is red because I put a beet in it.

en rødmen.explanation: "En rødmen" means "a blush". For the action, use the verb "at rødme" (to blush): "Hun rødmer, når han ser på hende" (She blushes when he looks at her).

sentence.da: Der kom en **rødmen** på hendes kinder, fordi hun var flov.
sentence.en: A blush came onto her cheeks because she was embarrassed.

en rødspætte.explanation: "En rødspætte" means "a plaice". The name starts with "rød" (red), for the orange-red spots on the fish. In Denmark, fried plaice is a traditional dish.

sentence.da: Til frokost spiser vi stegt **rødspætte** med remoulade.
sentence.en: For lunch we eat fried plaice with remoulade.

en rødvin.explanation: "En rødvin" means "a red wine". It is built from "rød" (red) and "vin" (wine). To say a glass of it, Danish has no word for "of": "et glas rødvin" (a glass of red wine).

sentence.da: **Rødvin** er lavet af mørke druer.
sentence.en: Red wine is made of dark grapes.

en røgalarm.explanation: "En røgalarm" means "a smoke alarm". It is built from "røg" (smoke) and "alarm" (alarm). To say it needs a new battery: "Røgalarmen skal have nyt batteri" (The smoke alarm needs a new battery).

sentence.da: En **røgalarm** bipper, når der er røg.
sentence.en: A smoke alarm beeps when there is smoke.

en røremaskine.explanation: "En røremaskine" means "a stand mixer". It is built from "at røre" (to stir) and "en maskine" (a machine). To say you whip cream with it: "Jeg pisker fløde i røremaskinen" (I whip cream in the stand mixer).

sentence.da: Jeg laver kagedej i min **røremaskine**.
sentence.en: I make cake batter in my stand mixer.

en røver.explanation: "En røver" means "a robber", a person who uses force or threats. Do not mix it up with "en tyv" (a thief), who steals without force: "Tyven tog min cykel" (The thief took my bike).

sentence.da: En **røver** truede kassedamen og tog alle pengene.
sentence.en: A robber threatened the cashier and took all the money.

et rat.explanation: "Et rat" means "a steering wheel". Do not mix it up with "et hjul" (a wheel that rolls on the ground): "Bilen har fire hjul" (The car has four wheels).

sentence.da: Man styrer bilen med et **rat**.
sentence.en: You steer the car with a steering wheel.

et realkreditlån.explanation: "Et realkreditlån" means "a mortgage". It is built from "realkredit" (mortgage credit) and "et lån" (a loan). In Denmark, the loan comes from "et realkreditinstitut" (a mortgage credit institution). To say you take one out: "Vi optager et realkreditlån" (We are taking out a mortgage).

sentence.da: Huset er købt med et **realkreditlån**, som vi betaler af hver måned.
sentence.en: The house was bought with a mortgage that we pay off every month.

et reb.explanation: "Et reb" means "a rope". A thinner cord is "en snor" (a string): "Hun bandt pakken med en snor" (She tied the package with a string). To say you skip rope: "Børnene hopper i reb" (The children are skipping rope).

sentence.da: Han bandt båden fast med et **reb**.
sentence.en: He tied up the boat with a rope.

et referat.explanation: "Et referat" means "a summary". For a meeting, it is the written minutes. To say you write them: "at skrive referat" (to write the minutes). The word comes from the verb "at referere" (to report).

sentence.da: Efter mødet sender hun et **referat** til alle.
sentence.en: After the meeting, she sends the minutes to everyone.

et regeringsparti.explanation: "Et regeringsparti" means "a governing party". It is built from "regering" (government) and "parti" (party). To name a party outside the government: "Et oppositionsparti kritiserer regeringen" (An opposition party criticizes the government).

sentence.da: Et **regeringsparti** har ministre og er med til at styre landet.
sentence.en: A governing party has ministers and helps run the country.

et regnskab.explanation: "Et regnskab" means "accounts". To say someone does a company's accounts: "Han laver regnskab for firmaet" (He does the accounts for the company). The accounts for a whole year are "et årsregnskab" (annual accounts).

sentence.da: Revisoren tjekker firmaets **regnskab**, så alle tal passer.
sentence.en: The auditor checks the company's accounts so that all the numbers add up.

et rejsebureau.explanation: "Et rejsebureau" means "a travel agency". It is built from "rejse" (trip) and "bureau" (office). To say you will phone one: "Jeg ringer til rejsebureauet" (I will call the travel agency).

sentence.da: Vi bestiller ferien på et **rejsebureau** i byen.
sentence.en: We are booking the vacation at a travel agency in town.

et rejsekort.explanation: "Et rejsekort" means "a travel card". In Denmark, it is the card for buses, trains and the metro. To remind someone to tap out when they get off: "Husk at checke ud" (Remember to check out).

sentence.da: Jeg checker ind med mit **rejsekort** i bussen.
sentence.en: I check in with my travel card on the bus.

et rejsemål.explanation: "Et rejsemål" means "a destination". It is built from "rejse" (trip) and "mål" (goal). To ask where someone is going: "Hvad er jeres rejsemål?" (What is your destination?)

sentence.da: Vores næste **rejsemål** er en lille by i Italien.
sentence.en: Our next destination is a small town in Italy.

et rektangel.explanation: "Et rektangel" means "a rectangle". The spelling differs from English: Danish has "k" where English has "c", and ends in "gel". The "e" drops when the word grows, as in "rektanglet" (the rectangle) and "rektangler" (rectangles).

sentence.da: Skærmen på min telefon er et **rektangel**.
sentence.en: The screen on my phone is a rectangle.

et rengøringsmiddel.explanation: "Et rengøringsmiddel" means "a cleaning product". It is built from "rengøring" (cleaning) and "et middel" (a product). To ask in a shop: "Hvor er rengøringsmidlerne?" (Where are the cleaning products?)

sentence.da: Med et **rengøringsmiddel** kan jeg gøre badeværelset rent.
sentence.en: With a cleaning product I can clean the bathroom.

et renseri.explanation: "Et renseri" means "a dry cleaner's". It comes from the verb "at rense" (to clean). To say you take a coat there: "Jeg afleverer jakken på renseriet" (I drop the jacket off at the dry cleaner's).

sentence.da: Fordi jakken ikke tåler vand, skal den på et **renseri**.
sentence.en: Because the jacket cannot take water, it has to go to a dry cleaner's.

et repertoire.explanation: "Et repertoire" means "a repertoire". To say what music a singer can perform: "Hendes repertoire omfatter både jazz og blues" (Her repertoire includes both jazz and blues).

sentence.da: Koret har et stort **repertoire** med både gamle og nye sange.
sentence.en: The choir has a large repertoire with both old and new songs.

et resultat.explanation: "Et resultat" means "a result". To say the score of a match: "Resultatet blev 2-1" (The result was 2-1).

sentence.da: Vi fik et godt **resultat** på prøven.
sentence.en: We got a good result on the test.

et resumé.explanation: "Et resumé" means "a summary". Do not use it for a job application. For that, Danish uses the short word "CV" (a résumé): "Send dit CV" (Send your résumé).

sentence.da: Til sidst i rapporten står et **resumé** af de vigtigste punkter.
sentence.en: At the end of the report there is a summary of the most important points.

et ribben.explanation: "Et ribben" means "a rib". It is also in "ribbensteg" (roast pork with crackling), built from "ribben" and "en steg" (a roast). Roast pork with crackling is a traditional Danish Christmas dish.

sentence.da: Et **ribben** er en buet knogle på siden af brystkassen.
sentence.en: A rib is a curved bone on the side of the chest.

et ritual.explanation: "Et ritual" means "a ritual". To say a daily habit is a ritual for you: "Morgenkaffen er et ritual for mig" (The morning coffee is a ritual for me).

sentence.da: Et **ritual** gentages på præcis samme måde hver gang.
sentence.en: A ritual is repeated in exactly the same way every time.

et rivejern.explanation: "Et rivejern" means "a grater". It is built from "at rive" (to grate) and "jern" (iron). To say you grate cheese: "Jeg river osten" (I grate the cheese).

sentence.da: Jeg bruger et **rivejern** til osten.
sentence.en: I use a grater for the cheese.

et rovdyr.explanation: "Et rovdyr" means "a predator". It is built from "rov" (loot) and "dyr" (animal). The same "rov" is in "en rovfugl" (a bird of prey).

sentence.da: Ulven er et **rovdyr**, men koen spiser kun græs.
sentence.en: The wolf is a predator, but the cow only eats grass.

et rum.explanation: "Et rum" means "a room or space". To talk about outer space, use "verdensrummet" (outer space). To say there is room for someone, use "plads" (room) instead: "Der er plads til os" (There is room for us).

sentence.da: Der er et stort **rum** ved siden af køkkenet.
sentence.en: There is a big room next to the kitchen.

et rumfang.explanation: "Et rumfang" means "a volume", as in the amount of space. For how loud a sound is, use "lydstyrke" (loudness) instead: "Skru lydstyrken op" (Turn the volume up).

sentence.da: Beregn kassens **rumfang**, når du kender længde, bredde og højde.
sentence.en: Calculate the box's volume when you know the length, width and height.

et rumskib.explanation: "Et rumskib" means "a spaceship". It is built from "rum" (space) and "et skib" (a ship). To say a spaceship takes off: "Rumskibet letter" (The spaceship takes off).

sentence.da: Et **rumskib** kan flyve til andre planeter.
sentence.en: A spaceship can fly to other planets.

et rumvæsen.explanation: "Et rumvæsen" means "an alien". It is built from "rum" (space) and "et væsen" (a being). To ask what someone believes: "Tror du på rumvæsener?" (Do you believe in aliens?)

sentence.da: Et **rumvæsen** er en skabning, der kommer fra en anden planet.
sentence.en: An alien is a creature that comes from another planet.

et rundstykke.explanation: "Et rundstykke" means "a bread roll". It is built from "rund" (round) and "et stykke" (a piece). To order at a bakery: "Jeg vil gerne have to rundstykker" (I would like two rolls).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser et **rundstykke** med ost.
sentence.en: I eat a bread roll with cheese.

et ry.explanation: "Et ry" means "a reputation". To say someone is known for something: "Han har ry for at være stædig" (He has a reputation for being stubborn).

sentence.da: Hotellet har fået et godt **ry**, fordi personalet er venligt.
sentence.en: The hotel has gotten a good reputation because the staff is friendly.

et rygte.explanation: "Et rygte" means "a rumor". To say people are talking about something: "Der går et rygte om, at butikken lukker" (There is a rumor that the store is closing).

sentence.da: Hun spreder et **rygte** om sin nabo.
sentence.en: She is spreading a rumor about her neighbor.

et råd.explanation: "Et råd" means "a piece of advice". The same word is in the phrase "at have råd til" (to be able to afford). To say you cannot afford something, use "råd" without "et": "Jeg har ikke råd til det" (I cannot afford it).

sentence.da: Må jeg give dig et **råd**?
sentence.en: May I give you a piece of advice?

et rådhus.explanation: "Et rådhus" means "a town hall". It is built from "råd" (council) and "et hus" (a house).

sentence.da: Det gamle **rådhus** ligger midt i byen.
sentence.en: The old town hall is in the middle of town.

et rådyr.explanation: "Et rådyr" means "a roe deer". The ending is "dyr" (animal), as in "et rovdyr" (a predator).

sentence.da: Et **rådyr** har lange ben og kan springe højt over hegn.
sentence.en: A roe deer has long legs and can jump high over fences.

et rækkehus.explanation: "Et rækkehus" means "a townhouse". It is built from "række" (row) and "hus" (house). To say where you live: "Vi bor i rækkehus" (We live in a townhouse).

sentence.da: I et **rækkehus** deler man væg med naboerne.
sentence.en: In a townhouse you share a wall with the neighbors.

et røntgenbillede.explanation: "Et røntgenbillede" means "an X-ray image". It is built from "røntgen", named after the German scientist Wilhelm Röntgen, who discovered X-rays, and "et billede" (a picture). To say a doctor takes one: "Lægen tager et røntgenbillede af min arm" (The doctor takes an X-ray of my arm).

sentence.da: Man kan se knoglerne inde i kroppen på et **røntgenbillede**.
sentence.en: You can see the bones inside the body on an X-ray.

et rør.explanation: "Et rør" means "a pipe". To say the water pipe has burst: "Røret er sprunget" (The pipe has burst).

sentence.da: Vandet løber gennem et **rør** under gulvet.
sentence.en: The water runs through a pipe under the floor.

et røveri.explanation: "Et røveri" means "a robbery". It comes from "en røver" (a robber). To say someone committed one: "Han begik et røveri" (He committed a robbery).

sentence.da: Der var et **røveri** i butikken i går.
sentence.en: There was a robbery in the store yesterday.

radikal.explanation: "Radikal" means "radical". To say a change for the better is big: "en radikal forbedring" (a radical improvement).

sentence.da: Regeringen vil lave en **radikal** reform, som ændrer hele skattesystemet.
sentence.en: The government wants to make a radical reform that changes the whole tax system.

raps.explanation: "En raps" means "rapeseed". To say rapeseed grows somewhere, leave out "en": "Der gror raps på marken" (Rapeseed is growing in the field).

sentence.da: Markerne bliver helt gule, når **raps** blomstrer om foråret.
sentence.en: The fields turn completely yellow when rapeseed blooms in the spring.

rar.explanation: "Rar" means "nice". To say you are glad to meet someone: "Rart at møde dig" (Nice to meet you). To say a moment was pleasant: "Det var rart at se dig" (It was nice to see you).

sentence.da: Din nabo er meget **rar**, og han hjælper os ofte.
sentence.en: Your neighbor is very nice, and he often helps us.

rasende.explanation: "Rasende" means "furious". It comes from the verb "at rase" (to rage). For light annoyance, use "irriteret" (annoyed): "Jeg er irriteret" (I am annoyed).

sentence.da: Han var **rasende**, fordi bilen var væk.
sentence.en: He was furious because the car was gone.

rask.explanation: "Rask" means "healthy", as in not ill. To say you get well after an illness: "at blive rask" (to get well). For food or habits that are good for you, use "sund" (healthy): "Frugt er sundt" (Fruit is healthy).

sentence.da: Du bliver **rask** igen.
sentence.en: You will get well again.

rastløs.explanation: "Rastløs" means "restless". It is built from "en rast" (a break) and "-løs" (without), so it is literally "without a break". To say how you feel: "Jeg føler mig rastløs" (I feel restless).

sentence.da: Efter flere uger uden arbejde blev han **rastløs** og ville ud.
sentence.en: After several weeks without work he became restless and wanted to get out.

rationel.explanation: "Rationel" means "rational". To say a method is efficient: "en rationel arbejdsgang" (an efficient way of working).

sentence.da: Hun er meget **rationel** og vælger altid ud fra fakta, ikke følelser.
sentence.en: She is very rational and always chooses based on facts, not feelings.

rav.explanation: "Et rav" means "amber". To say what something is made of: "Ringen er lavet af rav" (The ring is made of amber).

sentence.da: Man finder ofte **rav** på stranden efter en storm.
sentence.en: You often find amber on the beach after a storm.

realistisk.explanation: "Realistisk" means "realistic". English ends in "-ic", but Danish ends in "-isk". To say a film looks like real life: "Filmen er meget realistisk" (The film is very realistic).

sentence.da: Det er ikke **realistisk** at nå hele vejen på en time.
sentence.en: It is not realistic to make it the whole way in an hour.

regelmæssigt.explanation: "Regelmæssigt" means "regularly". It comes from "en regel" (a rule). To say you do something at steady times: "Jeg ringer regelmæssigt til min mor" (I call my mother regularly). Do not mix it up with "ofte" (often), which gives no steady pattern: "Jeg træner ofte, men ikke hver mandag" (I exercise often, but not every Monday).

sentence.da: Du skal motionere **regelmæssigt**, hvis du vil blive stærkere.
sentence.en: You must exercise regularly if you want to become stronger.

registreret.explanation: "Registreret" means "registered". It comes from the verb "at registrere" (to register). For registered mail, Danish uses "anbefalet" (recommended): "et anbefalet brev" (a registered letter).

sentence.da: Bilen er **registreret** i Danmark, så den har danske nummerplader.
sentence.en: The car is registered in Denmark, so it has Danish license plates.

regn.explanation: "Regn" means "rain". To say it is raining, use the verb: "Det regner" (It is raining). Danish does not say "Det er regn".

sentence.da: Der kommer meget **regn** i dag.
sentence.en: A lot of rain is coming today.

regnfuld.explanation: "Regnfuld" means "rainy". It is built from "regn" (rain) and "-fuld" (full of), as in "fredfuld" (peaceful). To say a week was rainy: "Det har været en regnfuld uge" (It has been a rainy week).

sentence.da: Det blev en **regnfuld** sommer, så vi var mest indendørs.
sentence.en: It became a rainy summer, so we were mostly indoors.

regnfuldt.explanation: "Regnfuldt" means "rainy". It is built from "regn" (rain) and "-fuldt" (full of). To say it is raining right now, use the verb: "Det regner" (It is raining).

sentence.da: Vejret har været **regnfuldt** hele ugen.
sentence.en: The weather has been rainy all week.

regntøj.explanation: "Regntøj" means "rain gear". It is built from "regn" (rain) and "tøj" (clothes). This word has no article, so you say it without "et": "Tag regntøj på" (Put on rain gear).

sentence.da: Børnene har **regntøj** på, fordi det regner.
sentence.en: The children are wearing rain gear because it is raining.

regnvejr.explanation: "Regnvejr" means "rainy weather". It is built from "regn" (rain) and "vejr" (weather). To say rain is falling right now, use the verb: "Det regner" (It is raining).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en paraply med i **regnvejr**.
sentence.en: I bring an umbrella in rainy weather.

rejer.explanation: "Rejer" means "shrimp". It is the plural of "en reje" (a shrimp). To say a sandwich with shrimp: "en rejemad" (a shrimp sandwich), built from "reje" and "mad" (food).

sentence.da: Jeg spiser gerne fisk og **rejer** fra havet.
sentence.en: I like eating fish and shrimp from the sea.

relativt.explanation: "Relativt" means "relatively". It is weaker than "meget" (very): "relativt dyr" (relatively expensive) says less than "meget dyr" (very expensive).

sentence.da: Prisen er **relativt** lav, når man tænker på kvaliteten.
sentence.en: The price is relatively low when you think about the quality.

relevant.explanation: "Relevant" means "relevant". To say something does not matter for the topic: "Det er ikke relevant" (That is not relevant).

sentence.da: Dit spørgsmål er **relevant**, men vi har ikke tid.
sentence.en: Your question is relevant, but we do not have time.

religiøs.explanation: "Religiøs" means "religious". It comes from "en religion" (a religion). To say a person has faith, you can also use "troende" (a believer): "Hun er troende" (She is a believer).

sentence.da: Jul er en **religiøs** højtid for kristne, men mange fejrer den alligevel.
sentence.en: Christmas is a religious holiday for Christians, but many celebrate it anyway.

remoulade.explanation: "En remoulade" means "a remoulade". In Denmark, it is served with fried fish and on hot dogs.

sentence.da: **Remoulade** er en kold sauce med små agurker.
sentence.en: Remoulade is a cold sauce with small pickles.
