ren.explanation: "Ren" means "clean". It also means "pure": "rent vand" (pure water). To say you clean a room, use "at gøre rent" (to clean): "Jeg gør rent i stuen" (I clean the living room).

sentence.da: Luften i skoven er **ren**.
sentence.en: The air in the forest is clean.

reserveret.explanation: "Reserveret" means "reserved". It comes from the verb "at reservere" (to reserve). To say a person is shy and keeps their distance: "Han er lidt reserveret" (He is a bit reserved).

sentence.da: Bordet er **reserveret** til os.
sentence.en: The table is reserved for us.

respekt.explanation: "Respekt" means "respect". Danish spells the ending "kt", where English has "ct". To say you respect your boss: "Han har stor respekt for sin chef" (He has great respect for his boss).

sentence.da: Børn skal lære at vise **respekt** for ældre.
sentence.en: Children must learn to show respect for older people.

resten.explanation: "Resten" means "the rest". To say you will do the remaining part later: "Jeg tager resten i morgen" (I will take the rest tomorrow). Do not mix it up with "rester" (leftovers): "Vi spiser rester" (We eat leftovers).

sentence.da: Du kan få **resten** af kagen.
sentence.en: You can have the rest of the cake.

rester.explanation: "Rester" means "leftovers". For one small bit that remains, use "en rest" (a leftover): "Der er en rest af kagen" (There is a bit of the cake left).

sentence.da: I dag spiser vi **rester** fra middagen i går.
sentence.en: Today we eat leftovers from yesterday's dinner.

retfærdig.explanation: "Retfærdig" means "fair". The opposite is "uretfærdig" (unfair): "Det er uretfærdigt" (That is unfair). Danish also borrows the English word "fair": "Det er ikke fair" (That is not fair).

sentence.da: Læreren er **retfærdig** og giver alle de samme chancer.
sentence.en: The teacher is fair and gives everyone the same chances.

retfærdighed.explanation: "En retfærdighed" means "justice". To talk about justice in general, leave out "en": "Der skal være retfærdighed" (There must be justice). The matching word for a decision is "retfærdig" (fair): "en retfærdig dom" (a fair verdict).

sentence.da: **Retfærdighed** betyder, at alle behandles ens.
sentence.en: Justice means that everyone is treated equally.

retskrivning.explanation: "En retskrivning" means "spelling rules". It is built from "ret" (correct) and "skrivning" (writing). In Denmark, the official spelling rules are in "Retskrivningsordbogen" (the spelling dictionary).

sentence.da: Reglerne i dansk **retskrivning** hjælper os med at stave rigtigt.
sentence.en: The rules of Danish spelling help us spell correctly.

retssikkerhed.explanation: "En retssikkerhed" means "a legal certainty". It is built from "rets" (of the law) and "sikkerhed" (security). To say a reform makes people safer under the law: "Reformen styrker retssikkerheden" (The reform strengthens legal certainty).

related.en: a state under the rule of law

sentence.da: Uden **retssikkerhed** kan man blive straffet uden en fair rettergang.
sentence.en: Without legal certainty, you can be punished without a fair trial.

ridning.explanation: "Ridning" means "horse riding". It comes from the verb "at ride" (to ride). To say you went on one outing: "Vi tog på en ridetur" (We went on a ride).

sentence.da: Til **ridning** skal man bruge en hest og en hjelm.
sentence.en: For horse riding you need a horse and a helmet.

rig.explanation: "Rig" means "rich". To say someone has a lot of something other than money: "rig på erfaring" (rich in experience). Do not mix it up with "et rige" (a kingdom): "Kongen styrer et stort rige" (The king rules a large kingdom).

sentence.da: Han er meget **rig** og har mange penge.
sentence.en: He is very rich and has a lot of money.

rigdom.explanation: "En rigdom" means "a wealth". To say there are many details: "en rigdom af detaljer" (a wealth of details).

sentence.da: Landets **rigdom** kommer fra olie og fiskeri.
sentence.en: The country's wealth comes from oil and fishing.

rigeligt.explanation: "Rigeligt" means "plenty". To politely turn down more: "Mere kaffe?" "Nej tak, jeg har rigeligt." (More coffee? No thanks, I have plenty.)

sentence.da: Vi har **rigeligt** med mad, så alle kan blive mætte.
sentence.en: We have plenty of food, so everyone can get full.

rigtig.explanation: "Rigtig" means "real". To say something is correct: "det rigtige svar" (the right answer). Before another describing word it means "really": "rigtig god" (really good).

sentence.da: Ja, din løsning er **rigtig**!
sentence.en: Yes, your solution is correct!

rimelig.explanation: "Rimelig" means "reasonable". To say you do not think something is fair: "Det er ikke rimeligt" (That is not reasonable).

sentence.da: Prisen på hotellet er **rimelig**, og værelset er stort.
sentence.en: The price of the hotel is reasonable, and the room is big.

ris.explanation: "Ris" means "rice". At Christmas in Denmark, the dessert "risalamande" (rice pudding with almonds) is made with rice.

sentence.da: Jeg koger **ris** og laver kylling til aftensmad.
sentence.en: I boil rice and make chicken for dinner.

risengrød.explanation: "En risengrød" means "a rice porridge". It is built from "ris" (rice) and "en grød" (a porridge). The cold Christmas dessert made from it is "risalamande" (rice pudding with almonds): "Til jul får vi risalamande" (At Christmas we have risalamande).

sentence.da: Til frokost spiser vi **risengrød** med smør, sukker og kanel.
sentence.en: For lunch we eat rice porridge with butter, sugar and cinnamon.

risikabel.explanation: "Risikabel" means "risky". It is built from "en risiko" (a risk). Do not use it for something that can hurt you. To say a dog is dangerous, use "farlig" (dangerous): "en farlig hund" (a dangerous dog).

sentence.da: Det er en **risikabel** plan, for vi kan miste alle pengene.
sentence.en: It is a risky plan, because we could lose all the money.

ro.explanation: "Ro" means "calm or peace and quiet". To say you find peace, use "at finde ro" (to find peace): "Jeg finder ro i skoven" (I find peace in the forest). To tell someone to relax, say "Slap af" (Relax).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne have **ro**, når jeg læser.
sentence.en: I would like some peace and quiet when I read.

robust.explanation: "Robust" means "robust". When you describe a bag that does not break easily, say: "en robust rygsæk" (a sturdy backpack). When you describe a person who does not get sick or upset easily, say: "Hun er robust" (She is tough).

sentence.da: Telefonen er **robust**, så den kan tåle et fald.
sentence.en: The phone is robust, so it can survive a fall.

rock.explanation: "Rock" means "rock" as in music. To name a show of this music, put "rock" in front of "koncert" (concert): "en rockkoncert" (a rock concert). For the stone, say "en sten" (a stone): "Der ligger en sten på vejen" (There is a stone in the road).

sentence.da: Jeg elsker **rock** med høje guitarer og trommer.
sentence.en: I love rock with loud guitars and drums.

rodet.explanation: "Rodet" means "messy". It is about things lying around, not dirt. To say a room is messy but clean, say: "Rummet er rodet, men ikke snavset" (The room is messy, but not dirty).

sentence.da: Børneværelset er meget **rodet** i dag.
sentence.en: The children's room is very messy today.

rolig.explanation: "Rolig" means "calm". To tell someone to stay calm, say: "Vær rolig" (Stay calm). To describe a quiet street, say: "en rolig gade" (a quiet street). To say how to speak, use the form "roligt": "Tal roligt" (Speak calmly).

sentence.da: Peter er helt **rolig** og smiler.
sentence.en: Peter is completely calm and smiling.

romantik.explanation: "Romantik" means "romance". To say a chore has no romance, say: "Der er ikke meget romantik i at vaske op" (There is not much romance in doing the dishes).

sentence.da: Levende lys og blomster giver **romantik**.
sentence.en: Candles and flowers bring romance.

romantisk.explanation: "Romantisk" means "romantic". It is built on "romantik" (romance). To describe a dinner for two, say: "en romantisk middag" (a romantic dinner).

sentence.da: Det er **romantisk** at gå en tur ved havet.
sentence.en: It is romantic to go for a walk by the sea.

roning.explanation: "Roning" means "rowing". It is the noun for "at ro" (to row), and a person who does it is "en roer" (a rower).

forms.en: to do rowing (as a club sport)

sentence.da: Til **roning** bruger man årer og sin egen muskelkraft.
sentence.en: For rowing you use oars and your own muscle power.

ros.explanation: "Ros" means "praise". To say someone deserves praise, say: "Hun fortjener ros" (She deserves praise).

sentence.da: Hun fik meget **ros** for sit arbejde.
sentence.en: She got a lot of praise for her work.

rug.explanation: "En rug" means "rye". To name the bread made from it, add "brød" (bread): "rugbrød" (rye bread).

sentence.da: Mel af **rug** gør brødet mørkt og tungt.
sentence.en: Flour made from rye makes the bread dark and heavy.

rugbrød.explanation: "Rugbrød" means "rye bread". It is built from "rug" (rye) and "brød" (bread). In Denmark, "smørrebrød" (open sandwiches) are traditionally made on a slice of it.

sentence.da: Jeg lægger ost på en skive **rugbrød**.
sentence.en: I put cheese on a slice of rye bread.

rummelig.explanation: "Rummelig" means "spacious". It is built on "et rum" (a room, a space). To describe a bag with a lot of space, say: "en rummelig taske" (a spacious bag).

sentence.da: Bilen er **rummelig**, og der er plads til hele familien.
sentence.en: The car is spacious, and there is room for the whole family.

rund.explanation: "Rund" means "round". To say a number is round, say: "Hundrede er et rundt tal" (One hundred is a round number).

sentence.da: Jorden er **rund**, ikke flad.
sentence.en: The earth is round, not flat.

rundt om hjørnet.explanation: "Rundt om hjørnet" means "around the corner". To say a place is close, say: "Posthuset ligger rundt om hjørnet" (The post office is around the corner). To say a date is coming soon, say: "Julen er lige rundt om hjørnet" (Christmas is just around the corner).

forms.en: The bakery is around the corner.

forms.da: Butikken er lige rundt om hjørnet.
forms.en: The shop is just around the corner.

sentence.da: Banken ligger lige **rundt om hjørnet**.
sentence.en: The bank is just around the corner.

rusland.explanation: "Rusland" means "Russia". Use "i" (in) for being there and "til" (to) for going there: "Jeg bor i Rusland" (I live in Russia), "Jeg rejser til Rusland" (I am traveling to Russia).

sentence.da: Man taler russisk i **Rusland**.
sentence.en: People speak Russian in Russia.

russisk.explanation: "Russisk" means "Russian". To ask for a word in the language, use "på" (in): "Hvad hedder det på russisk?" (What is it called in Russian?). The country is "Rusland" (Russia).

sentence.da: Han kommer fra Rusland og taler **russisk**.
sentence.en: He comes from Russia and speaks Russian.

ryddelig.explanation: "Ryddelig" means "tidy". It comes from the verb "at rydde" (to clear). To say you tidy up, use "at rydde op" (to tidy up): "Jeg rydder op i stuen" (I am tidying up the living room).

sentence.da: Hendes lejlighed er altid **ryddelig** og pæn.
sentence.en: Her apartment is always tidy and nice.

rynket.explanation: "Rynket" means "wrinkled". It comes from "at rynke" (to wrinkle). To say you frown, use "at rynke panden" (literally, to wrinkle the forehead).

sentence.da: Skjorten er helt **rynket**, så jeg må stryge den.
sentence.en: The shirt is all wrinkled, so I have to iron it.

rystende.explanation: "Rystende" means "shocking". It comes from "at ryste" (to shake). When you describe hands that tremble, it means "trembling": "rystende hænder" (trembling hands).

sentence.da: Billederne fra ulykken var **rystende**, og mange græd.
sentence.en: The pictures from the accident were shocking, and many cried.

rystet.explanation: "Rystet" means "shaken". It comes from "at ryste" (to shake). To say news has upset you, use "over" (about): "Vi er alle rystede over nyheden" (We are all shaken by the news).

sentence.da: Hun var meget **rystet** efter den alvorlige ulykke på motorvejen.
sentence.en: She was very shaken after the serious accident on the highway.

rå.explanation: "Rå" means "raw". When you describe food that is not cooked, say: "rå fisk" (raw fish). When you describe harsh words, it means "crude": "et råt sprog" (crude language).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke lide **rå** løg.
sentence.en: I do not like raw onions.

rædselsslagen.explanation: "Rædselsslagen" means "terrified". It is built from "en rædsel" (a horror) and "slagen" (struck), so it is literally "struck by horror". It is much stronger than "bange" (afraid): "Jeg er bange for edderkopper" (I am afraid of spiders).

sentence.da: Hun blev **rædselsslagen**, da hun så slangen på gulvet.
sentence.en: She became terrified when she saw the snake on the floor.

rød.explanation: "Rød" means "red". It is the first part of words such as "rødvin" (red wine) and "rødbede" (beetroot).

sentence.da: Tomaten er **rød**.
sentence.en: The tomato is red.

rødgrød.explanation: "En rødgrød" means "red berry pudding". It is built from "rød" (red) and "grød" (porridge). Despite the ending "grød", it is a pudding, not a porridge.

forms.en: a bowl of red berry pudding

sentence.da: Til dessert fik vi kold **rødgrød** med fløde.
sentence.en: For dessert we had cold red berry pudding with cream.

rødhåret.explanation: "Rødhåret" means "red-haired". It is built from "rød" (red) and "hår" (hair). Other hair words are built the same way: "lyshåret" (fair-haired) and "mørkhåret" (dark-haired).

sentence.da: Min lillesøster er **rødhåret**, og hendes hår er næsten orange.
sentence.en: My little sister is red-haired, and her hair is almost orange.

røg.explanation: "Røg" means "smoke". When you name things that deal with smoke, "røg" is the first part of "røgalarm" (smoke alarm) and "røgfri" (smoke-free).

forms.en: There is smoke in the room.

sentence.da: Jeg kan se **røg** fra skorstenen.
sentence.en: I can see smoke from the chimney.

rørende.explanation: "Rørende" means "touching". It comes from "at røre" (to touch, to stir). To say you were moved yourself, use "rørt" (moved): "Jeg blev rørt" (I was moved).

sentence.da: Talen var **rørende**, og flere i salen græd.
sentence.en: The speech was touching, and several people in the hall cried.

rørsukker.explanation: "Rørsukker" means "cane sugar". It is built from "rør" (reed) and "sukker" (sugar).

sentence.da: **Rørsukker** laves af planten sukkerrør, som vokser i varme lande.
sentence.en: Cane sugar is made from the plant sugarcane, which grows in warm countries.

rørt.explanation: "Rørt" means "touched" as in feeling moved, not as in a hand on something. To say something moved someone to tears, say: "Han var rørt til tårer" (He was moved to tears).

sentence.da: Jeg blev så **rørt** over din gave.
sentence.en: I was so touched by your gift.

røræg.explanation: "Røræg" means "scrambled eggs". It is built from "at røre" (to stir) and "et æg" (an egg). To say you want fried eggs, use "spejlæg" (fried eggs): "Jeg vil have to spejlæg" (I would like two fried eggs).

sentence.da: Vi laver **røræg** med bacon til morgenmad.
sentence.en: We make scrambled eggs with bacon for breakfast.
